verdict: OK to lend in Kochi seafood processing, but only to processors with diversified buyer books and disciplined working capital; avoid single-buyer US-dependent units.
title: Kochi seafood processing & export: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Kochi shrimp processor buys raw shrimp from farms and landing centres, freezes and grades it, and ships containers to importers abroad. **Cash turns on the harvest-to-container cycle, not on the plant.** Value sits in cold-chain quality and buyer relationships; the plant is the cheap part. So when a proposal lands, check the cold-store capacity and the buyer list before the machinery list.

A rating note on a peer shows maximum working-capital utilisation at about 96% for the 12 months to June 30, 2025, with a temporary overdraft taken from lenders [10]. **That is the shape of the risk: fully drawn limits, not idle ones.** Ask every applicant for peak drawing power and the temporary-overdraft history; if utilisation sits near that level, ask what the buffer is.

## What has changed
Local news is mixed. Kochi port exports fell 10.4% between January and August, with West Asia war and US tariffs cited [3]. Against that, a March 2026 rating report says India's shrimp exports will cross Rs 50,000 crore this fiscal, up 13-15% on-year, as shippers move to other markets [9]. Peer results back the price story: Apex Frozen's Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%, on a 15% rise in average shrimp realisation with flat revenue [5][6]. **Realisation, not volume, is carrying the trade.** Note the older May 2025 rating view of flattish volumes and margin pressure [8]; treat it as history, not the current position.

## Where to grow
Pursue processors with spread buyer books across the US, Europe and Canada, and those adding domestic HoReCa and retail sales. The Kochi summit on November 4 brings European distributors and MPEDA officials together, with three agreements to be signed [1][2] — **use it to map which local borrowers have real European offtake, not just US.** Avoid units where one importer takes most of the book; a peer rating flags dependency on a single buyer group as a live risk [11].

## How to grow safely
Structure against the season: cash credit sized to peak stock, not to turnover, plus a term loan only for cold-chain assets. Take monthly stock-and-book-debt statements, monthly buyer-wise sales, and quarterly drawing-power certificates. **Covenant on peak utilisation and on buyer concentration.** Collect from customer the buyer-wise sales split and the peak stock value; these are not in our sources.

## Early warning signs
Watch for drawing power stuck near the ceiling with repeated temporary overdrafts [10], a falling share of non-US sales, and receivables stretching past agreed terms. If a borrower's top buyer crosses half of sales, ask for the contract and the payment history before renewal.
